programs.name: Civil Engineering BS
notes: 1 additional unit in biological sciences (200-level or higher), chemistry, or physics, or
1 unit of unrestricted electives is from Chemistry lab, PHYSICS 136-2 , and CIV_ENV 301-
300 level or higher in mathematics, science, engineering, or another area supporting the area of specialization. Choose from an approved list available in Undergraduate CIV_ENV Handbook.
4 courses chosen from the focus areas below

courses.title: Introduction to Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.desc: In this seminar course we discuss the grand challenges facing society in the coming decades, and how Civil and Environmental Engineers are meeting these challenges. Seminars will focus on key CE and EE topics, the CE & EE curricula at NU, and the career paths of recent CE & EE graduates.

courses.title: Cornerstone Design
courses.desc: Explore how civil and environmental engineers define problems, evaluate alternatives, and develop sustainable, ethical design solutions. Learn key components of engineering infrastructure systems and practice them using industry-standard modeling and analysis tools. Through integrated lab work and a team-based infrastructure project, students develop schematic designs supported by technical, economic, and community considerations.

courses.title: Biological and Ecological Principles
courses.desc: Fundamentals of biology - including cell biology, genetics, and biochemistry - and ecology - including biological interactions, microbial ecology - and biogeochemical cycling as they apply to natural and engineered systems. Bioinformatics tools necessary for analyzing biological and ecological data.
courses.text: Prerequisites: MATH 220-2 ; CHEM 131-0 , CHEM 151-0 , or CHEM 171-0 .

courses.title: Earth in the Anthropocene
courses.desc: Fundamentals of Earth system science and their connections to the need for humans to develop food, water, energy and infrastructure systems that has led to transformation of the Earth's surface and of its atmosphere.
courses.text: Prerequisite: MATH 220-2 ; CHEM 131-0 , CHEM 151-0 , or CHEM 171-0 is highly recommended.

courses.title: Economics and Finance for Engineers
courses.desc: Principles of corporate finance; financial decisions of firms; value; risk and return; investment and capital budgeting decisions under certainty and uncertainty; performance evaluation. May not be taken for credit with or after KELLG_FE 310-0.
courses.text: Prerequisite: MATH 220-1 ; basic understanding of probability and economics recommended.

offered.Fall 2026: TTh 3:30-4:50 · Pablo Texeira Manion · (Lab: W 4:00-4:50 or 12:00-12:50)

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials I
courses.desc: Analytical and experimental study of stresses and deformations and their application to the design of machine and structural elements subjected to static, dynamic, and repeated loads.

courses.title: Structural Art
courses.desc: Learn how to interpret and understand the built environment through an examination of the history of structural engineering as a creative art, with particular emphasis on technical, visual, and social analysis and critique of bridges, buildings, and designers.

courses.title: Theory of Structures I
courses.desc: Deflections of structures, energy concepts, idealization of structures, truss analysis, column stability, and influence lines. Introduction to indeterminate truss and frame analyses, slope-deflection analysis, and moment distribution. Portal method.

courses.title: Earth Surface Engineering
courses.desc: Fundamental properties and behavior of soils as engineering materials. Origin of soils through the properties of soil components to the strength, permeability, and deformation of soil masses.

courses.title: Environmental Systems and Processes
courses.desc: Basic engineering principles required for the design, operation, analysis, and modeling of both natural and engineered systems and their application to major issues facing human and environmental health of ecosystems.
courses.text: Corequisite: MATH 220-2 ; CHEM 131-0 , CHEM 151-0 , or CHEM 171-0 highly recommended.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering & Design Seminar I
courses.desc: First course in the AED seminar series. Students will learn from practicing architects and engineers, and will also conduct independent studies culminating in their own seminars to the class.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering & Design Seminar II
courses.desc: Second course in the AED seminar series. Students will learn from practicing architects and engineers, and will also conduct independent studies culminating in their own seminars to the class.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering & Design Seminar III
courses.desc: Third course in the AED seminar series. Students will learn from practicing architects and engineers, and will also conduct independent studies culminating in their own seminars to the class.

courses.title: Introductory topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
courses.desc: Intermediate-level study of topics suggested by students or faculty members and approved by the department.

courses.title: Cornerstone Design Lab
courses.desc: CIV_ENV 201-0 Lab component. Students develop familiarity with industry-standard modeling and analysis tools through developing schematic designs supported by technical, economic, and community considerations.

courses.title: Professional Development Seminar II
courses.desc: Preparation for the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam.

courses.title: Engineering Law
courses.desc: The American legal system from an engineer's perspective. Socratic-method analysis of statutory and case law. Contract, patent, corporation, antitrust, property, and environmental law. Torts, product liability, and arbitration.

courses.title: Environmental Law and Policy
courses.desc: An introduction to important aspects of environmental law and policy. Covers a wide range of environmental topics, with a focus on major federal environmental statutes.

courses.title: Civil and Environmental Engineering Systems Analysis
courses.desc: Quantitative techniques to develop descriptive and prescriptive models that support efficient planning and management of civil and environmental engineering systems.

courses.title: Uncertainty Analysis
courses.desc: Probability, statistics, and decision theory. Discrete and continuous random variables, marginal and conditional distributions, moments, statistical model selection and significance tests, hypothesis testing, and elementary Bayesian decision theory. Application to problems in soil mechanics, water resources, transportation, and structures.

courses.title: Environmental Justice
courses.desc: This course will examine evidence that there is not equal environmental protection in this country and analyze why this inequality exists. Course participants will review evidence of environmental injustice, with attention to perspectives of grassroots organizations, the U.S. EPA, and businesses. The course will explore why civil and human rights have become important aspects of environmental protection activities worldwide.

courses.title: Climate and Energy - Law and Policy
courses.desc: This course is a survey of the major laws that regulate the acquisition of energy resources, the conversion of energy resources into usable energy, the energy transmission and transportation infrastructure and the climate change implications of these activities.

courses.title: Organic Geochemistry
courses.desc: The sources and fates of organic matter in the natural environment; global cycling of organic carbon; applications to the study of modern and ancient environments. Taught with EARTH 314-0; may not receive credit for both courses.
courses.text: Prerequisites: 1 course in earth and planetary sciences or environmental sciences; 1 course in chemistry.

courses.title: Biogeochemistry
courses.desc: Cycling of biogenic elements (C, N, S, Fe, Mn) in surficial environments. Emphasis on microbial processes and isotopic signatures.
courses.text: Prerequisites: 1 quarter of chemistry; 1 quarter of geoscience, environmental sciences, or biological sciences.

courses.title: Structural Analysis--Dynamics
courses.desc: Single and multiple degree-of-freedom systems subjected to periodic, seismic, and general loadings. Time-history analysis of linear and nonlinear systems. Design methods for earthquakes.

courses.title: Concrete Properties
courses.desc: Concrete as a composite material; relationship between constitutive laws and microstructure; failure theories; fracture; fatigue; strain rate effects; destructive and nondestructive testing; creep and shrinkage; chemistry of cement hydration; admixtures; aggregates; proportioning; new materials.

courses.title: Structural Steel Design
courses.desc: Rational basis of structural design. Design approach for structural-steel components of a building system.

courses.title: Reinforced Concrete
courses.desc: Fundamentals of reinforced concrete theory and design. Analysis and design of beams, slabs, and columns. Concurrent familiarization with current building codes, specifications, and practices.

courses.title: Engineering Forensics
courses.desc: Introduction to failure analysis and forensic engineering to describe how these investigative procedures contribute to regulations, engineering design, safety principles, and the economic aspects of structure engineering.

courses.title: Finite Element Methods in Mechanics
courses.desc: Development of finite elements from variational principles and application to static stress analysis. Introduction to techniques for transient and generalized field problems. Computer implementation of finite element techniques. Taught with MECH_ENG 327-0; may not receive credit for both courses.

courses.title: Computational Forensics and Failure Analysis
courses.desc: The course will cover the use of the scientific method for accident investigation, hypothesis development, and the use of the finite element method to analyze the root cause of a failure. Practical application problems for both civil and mechanical structures will be analyzed using commercial finite element codes (Abaqus, Hypermesh, LS-Dyna) Prerequiste: CIV_ENV 327-0 or MECH_ENG 327-0.

courses.title: Engineering Project Management
courses.desc: Techniques for coordinating decisions and actions of various parties in the design and construction of civil and environmental engineering projects. Delivery systems; preconstruction services; project planning; cost control and value engineering; bidding.

courses.title: Ecohydrology
courses.desc: Interactions between water and ecosystems in freshwater, terrestrial, and urban environments. Feedbacks between ecological and hydrological processes. Engineering of ecosystems such as constructed wetlands, green roofs, and other green infrastructure for resilient and sustainable water management.
courses.text: Prerequisites:Students must have taken CIV_ENV 260, one course in fluid mechanics, or have graduate standing.

courses.title: Foundation Engineering
courses.desc: Application of soil mechanics to analysis and design of foundations and embankments. Settlement of structures, bearing capacities of shallow and deep foundations, earth pressures on retaining structures, and slope stability.

courses.title: Energy Geostructures & Geosystems
courses.desc: This course focuses on energy geostructures and geosystems: novel earth-contact technologies that provide renewable energy supply and structural support to any built environment. The course comprises theoretical and practical sessions. The theoretical sessions expand on the analysis and design of such technologies from energy, geotechnical and structural perspectives. The practical sessions simulate an actual design project of energy geostructures.

courses.title: Environmental Microbiology
courses.desc: Basic principles and practical applications of microbiology to environmental issues, such as microbial contamination, degradation of organic contaminants, production of alternative fuels, and global climate change.

courses.title: Public & Environmental Health
courses.desc: Current problems in public and environmental health, such as the worldwide burden of major infectious diseases, emergence of new pathogens, and environmental reservoirs of infectious organisms.
courses.text: Prerequisite: CIV_ENV 361-1 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Sustainable Water Systems
courses.desc: An overview of the engineered water cycle focusing the fundamental principles as well as the design and assessment methods for physical, chemical and biological treatment unit processes for drinking water treatment, used water treatment and reuse, and emerging issues such as the energy-food-water nexus.

courses.title: Environmental Laboratory
courses.desc: Chemical and microbiological aspects of environmental engineering and science are explored through an integrated laboratory course.

courses.title: Dynamics in Chemical Transport and Reaction
courses.desc: Application of environmental engineering fundamentals to evaluate, model, and develop engineering solutions for different environmental contamination scenarios.

courses.title: Chemical Processes in Aquatic Systems
courses.desc: Chemical principles for understanding and predicting the chemical composition and evolution of natural waters using an equilibrium approach. Applications to environmental issues such as metal speciation and toxicity, ocean acidification, carbon storage.

courses.title: Sustainability: The City
courses.desc: Exploration of the issues that motivate the design and engineering of sustainable resource use and development.

courses.title: Emerging Organic Contaminants
courses.desc: Fundamental molecular processes that govern the fate and transformation of emerging organic contaminants in natural and engineered environmental systems.
courses.text: Prerequisite: CHEM 210-1 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Transportation Planning and Analysis
courses.desc: Analysis and design of solutions to transportation problems; introduction to selected operations research and statistical analysis techniques; use of case studies in urban transportation, intercity passenger transport, and freight movements.
courses.text: Prerequisite: junior standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Science for Urban Systems
courses.desc: Introduces students to modern data science methodologies tailored for solving complex urban challenges, such as transportation systems, sustainable infrastructure, environmental monitoring, and smart cities.

courses.title: Transportation System Operations
courses.desc: Traffic-flow theory; vehicle and human factors, capacity analysis, intersection performance and control; management and control of arterial streets and networks; neighborhood traffic restraint, urban transit operations. Operations concepts and theories applied to actual problems through laboratory practice.
courses.text: Prerequisite: basic understanding of calculus and statistics; knowledge of MATLAB desirable but not required.

courses.title: Choice Modelling in Engineering
courses.desc: This course focuses on the theory and practice of survey design, data and analysis. In this course students will learn the theories and scientific debates around the design, administration and analysis of various types of behavioral data-collection methods."

courses.title: Capstone Design I
courses.desc: Culminating team-based design experience in civil and environmental engineering, with an overview of the function, design, and operations of modern infrastructure systems. Part 1 of 2-course sequence.
courses.text: Prerequisite: senior standing in civil or environmental engineering or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Capstone Design II
courses.desc: Culminating team-based design experience in civil and environmental engineering, with an overview of the function, design, and operations of modern infrastructure systems. Part 2 of 2-course sequence.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering and Design 1: Fundamentals
courses.desc: Architectural engineering and design studios: architectural history, case studies in design, construction and management of buildings, and drawing and model building. Fundamental studio: basic architectural and structural design of a simple building project.
courses.text: Prerequisite: junior standing in engineering or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering & Design 2: Intermediate
courses.desc: Architectural engineering and design studios: architectural history, case studies in design, construction and management of buildings, and drawing and model building. Intermediate studio: architectural and structural design of a building project with multiple requirements.
courses.text: Prerequisites: CIV_ENV 385-1 and junior standing in engineering; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Architectural Engineering & Design 3: Advanced Studio
courses.desc: Architectural engineering and design studios: architectural history, case studies in design, construction and management of buildings, and drawing and model building. Advanced studio: architectural and structural design of a large, complex building project.
courses.text: Prerequisites: CIV_ENV 385-2 and junior standing in engineering; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: High Performance Architectural Design
courses.desc: Elements of high performance building design and to explore the various matrics used to analyze the relationship between the structure and function of various design alternatives.

courses.title: Design of Sustainable Urban Developments
courses.desc: Design high performing neighborhoods, districts and communities that incorporate principles of density, diversity and flexibility around the "operating system of nature".
courses.text: Prerequisites: CIV_ENV 386-0 , senior standing, consent of instructor; recommend CIV_ENV 385-1 , CIV_ENV 385-2 , and CIV_ENV 385-3 .

courses.title: Building Science I: Fundamentals for Sustainable Buildings
courses.desc: The course is the first of a two-part series focusing on Building Science. This course aims to provide the fundamental knowledge of the physics related to buildings, focusing on heat and mass transfer, moisture, and the energy consumed in buildings to guarantee the comfort of their occupants.

courses.title: Building Science II: Application for Sustainable Buildings
courses.desc: This course enriches and applies the concepts learned in CIV_ENV 388-1. The course comprises both theoretical and practical sessions. Theoretical sessions introduce the environmental factors affecting occupants' comfort inside buildings. Practical sessions focus on the design of a virtual project, with calculations related to energy consumption and visual and thermal parameters with the help of computer software.

courses.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engrg
courses.desc: Topics suggested by students or faculty and approved by the department.

courses.title: Community-based Design 1
courses.desc: Yearlong participation in two-or three-person team projects involving research, analysis, and/or design in the solution of environmental problems affecting primarily lower-income communities. Grade assigned only on completion of both units.

courses.title: Community-based Design 2
courses.desc: Yearlong participation in two-or three-person team projects involving research, analysis, and/or design in the solution of environmental problems affecting primarily lower-income communities. Grade assigned only on completion of both units.

courses.title: Projects
courses.desc: Special studies under faculty direction. Credit to be arranged.

courses.title: Introduction to the History of Architecture: 1400 to Present
courses.desc: The theory and history of architecture in relation to cities and landscape; historical periods and regions of focus may vary depending on the instructor.

courses.title: Architecture & Landscapes, 1750?1890
courses.desc: The history and theory of architecture, especially in relation to cities and landscape, from 1750 to 1890.

courses.title: Architecture & Landscapes, 1890 to Present
courses.desc: The history and theory of architecture, especially in relation to cities and landscape, after 1890.

courses.title: The Global City
courses.desc: An examination of architecture, urbanism, and the city as a socioeconomic system; period and regions of focus vary. Past topics have included Ottoman Istanbul, Babylon, and Tenochtitlan-Mexico City.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.desc: Physical and chemical principles as applied to biological systems and medical devices. Topics include material balances, thermodynamics, solution chemistry, electrochemistry, surface chemistry, transport, and kinetics.
courses.text: Prerequisites: MATH 228-1 ; CHEM 132-0 , CHEM 152-0 , or CHEM 172-0 .

courses.title: Biomedical Engineering Design
courses.desc: Development of a design project initiated during the previous quarter.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemistry I
courses.desc: Quantum mechanics, electronic structure, periodic properties of elements, chemical bonding, thermodynamics, intermolecular forces, properties of solids and liquids, solutions and colligative properties.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemistry II
courses.desc: Chemical equilibrium, aqueous solution equilibria, chemical kinetics, metals in chemistry and biology, oxidation-reduction reactions and electrochemistry.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.desc: Chemical analysis of real samples using basic laboratory techniques including titration, colorimetric analysis, density measurements, and atomic spectroscopy. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 131-0.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.desc: Chemistry laboratory techniques applied to materials science and nanotechnology, acid-base chemistry, and chemical kinetics. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 132-0.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.desc: Quantum mechanics, electronic structure, periodic properties of elements, chemical bonding, thermodynamics, gas laws, intermolecular forces, properties of solids and liquids, solutions and colligative properties.
courses.text: Prerequisite: permission of department by placement exam.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.desc: Chemical equilibrium, aqueous solution equilibria, chemical kinetics, metals in chemistry and biology, oxidation-reduction reactions and electrochemistry.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.desc: Chemical analysis of real samples using basic laboratory techniques including titration, colorimetric analysis, density measurements, and atomic spectroscopy. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 151-0.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.desc: Chemistry laboratory techniques applied to materials science and nanotechnology, acid-base chemistry, and chemical kinetics. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 152-0.

courses.title: Advanced General Inorganic Chemistry
courses.desc: Review of mole problems and stoichiometry; descriptive chemistry, elements, compounds, and inorganic reactions; gas laws; phase equilibria and colligative properties; chemical equilibrium; aqueous equilibria; topics in chemical bonding and molecular structure. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 181-0.

courses.title: Advanced General Physical Chemistry
courses.desc: Thermodynamics and equilibrium; chemical kinetics and mechanism; electrochemistry; electronic structure of the atom and quantum theory; advanced topics in chemical bonding; coordination compounds; solid-state chemistry; nuclear chemistry. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 182-0.
courses.text: Prerequisites: CHEM 171-0 , CHEM 181-0 (C- or better); MATH 220-1 .

courses.title: Advanced General Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.desc: Laboratory techniques for studying chemical analysis and chemical reactions relevant to environmental or materials research. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 171-0.

courses.title: Advanced General Physical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.desc: Study of physical chemistry (acid base chemistry, thermodynamics, etc.) in the laboratory. Planning, data collection, interpretation, and reporting on these experiments. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 172-0.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.desc: Foundational concepts in organic chemistry will be introduced. Topics include structure and properties of common functional groups, acidity/basicity, conformational analysis, stereochemistry, and reactivity of organic compounds.
courses.text: Prerequisites: CHEM 132-0 and CHEM 142-0 , or CHEM 152-0 and CHEM 162-0 , or CHEM 172-0 and CHEM 182-0 (C- or better); or qualifying score on the Chemistry Placement Exam. Must be taken concurrently with CHEM 235-1 .

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.desc: The first and second laws of thermodynamics. Entropy and equilibrium. Material and energy balances. Equations of state and properties of fluids. Solutions, phase equilibria, and chemical reactions.

courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.desc: Theory, composition, delivery, and criticism of public speeches.

courses.title: Design Thinking and Communication
courses.desc: Integrated introduction to the user-centered design process and technical communication. Students will address challenges proposed by project partners by identifying unmet needs, conducting research, generating and evaluating potential solutions, and finally, presenting a final design concept with supporting documentation. Students also enhance their abilities in equitable teamwork, project management, fabrication skills, and producing written, oral, graphical, and interpersonal communication. One lecture, two section meetings, and lab. Co-registration with ENGLISH 106-1 required. Primarily intended for first-year engineering students.
courses.text: Prerequisite: Reserved for McCormick students only.

courses.title: Design Thinking and Communication
courses.desc: Integrated iteration on the user-centered design process and technical communication. This course will build on the learning objectives from DTC-1 while adding more focus on ethics in design and communication, equitable distribution of teamwork, project management, documenting and communicating progress, and exploring a wider variety of project topics. One lecture, two section meetings, and lab. Co-registration with ENGLISH 106-2 required. Primarily intended for first-year engineering students.

courses.title: Physical Earth Science
courses.desc: Physical Earth Science synthesizes physical geology and historical geology. Physical geology examines the creation, modification, and characterization of rocks and minerals, as well as internal and external processes that shape the planet. Historical geology examines the origin and evolution of Earth and life through time. The course includes required laboratory sections and culminates with a required weekend field trip.

courses.title: Physics of the Earth's Interior
courses.desc: The earth as a planet: origin, composition, and evolution of the solar system and the earth; internal structure of the earth; plate tectonics. Recommended Background: At least one credit in math, chemistry, biology or physics.

courses.title: Writing in Special Contexts
courses.desc: Introduction to expository writing similar to ENGLISH 105-0 but paired with a course in another discipline.

courses.title: Writing in Special Contexts
courses.desc: Introduction to expository writing similar to ENGLISH 105-0 but paired with a course in another discipline.

courses.title: Principles of Entrepreneurship
courses.desc: This course serves as the foundational course for the undergraduate minor in entrepreneurship. This survey-style course is a good choice for students who wish to familiarize themselves with the world of entrepreneurship. Students will learn to think like entrepreneurs and will be introduced to key topics relevant to entrepreneurship, including customer discovery, finance, and marketing. They will also learn how to understand and perform analyses of a broad range of entrepreneurial activities related to different applications of entrepreneurship. Taught with IEMS 225-0; may not receive credit for both courses.

courses.title: Engineering Entrepreneurship
courses.desc: The goal of the course is to introduce students to innovation-driven entrepreneurship, a process by which emergent technology serves as the catalyst for new venture formation. This course challenges student teams to develop strategies for commercializing cutting-edge technologies. Each year, the course focuses on a significant innovation space. Taught with IEMS 325-0; may not receive credit for both courses.

courses.title: Programming for Engineers
courses.desc: Object-Oriented Programming including Programming Basics (Data abstraction, Simple procedures, Primitive data), Procedural Programming Fundamentals (Conditional Execution, Iteration, Recursion, Modularity and Procedural abstraction, Composite data - lists, dictionaries), and Object-Oriented Principles (Composite data -classes, Encapsulation, Inheritance). Students may receive credit for only one of: COMP_SCI 150, GEN_ENG 150, and GEN_ENG 151.

courses.title: Honors Programming for Engineers
courses.desc: Object-Oriented Programming including Programming Basics (Data abstraction, Simple procedures, Primitive data), Procedural Programming Fundamentals (Conditional Execution, Iteration, Recursion, Modularity and Procedural abstraction, Composite data - lists, dictionaries), and Object-Oriented Principles (Composite data -classes, Encapsulation, Inheritance). The honors section will include students who received a 4 or 5 on AP CS A.
courses.text: Prerequisite: COMP_SCI 1CA or instructor permission. Students may not receive credit for both GEN_ENG 151-0 and COMP_SCI 150-0 or GEN_ENG 150-0 .

courses.title: Engineering Analysis II
courses.desc: Linear algebra and introduction to vector methods in engineering analysis. Statics and dynamics of rigid bodies and matrix analysis of trusses and networks. Engineering design problems.
courses.text: Prerequisites: C- or better in GEN_ENG 205-1 ; MATH 220-1 .

courses.title: Honors Engineering Analysis
courses.desc: Covers topics addressed in GEN_ENG 205-2 at a deeper level. Intended for students with demonstrated strength in mathematics, computer programming, and/or physics.

courses.title: Engineering Physics - Statics
courses.desc: Introduction to vector methods in engineering analysis. Statics of particles and rigid bodies and matrix analysis of trusses and frames. Engineering design problems.
courses.text: Prerequisites: Gen_Eng 150, Gen_Eng 151 or Comp_Sci 150 (Programming), Math 220-1 or equivalent.

courses.title: Engineering Physics - Dynamics
courses.desc: A calculus-based physics course which emphasizes dynamic analysis techniques relevant to solving engineering problems in the mechanical domain. This course introduces Newtonian mechanics, descriptions of relative motion in Cartesian and polar coordinate systems, energy conservation methods, mechanical power, momentum, impulse, and numerical and analytical methods for describing oscillatory systems.
courses.text: Prerequisites: Math 220-2 or equivalent, GEN_ENG 211, GEN_ENG 241 or equivalent (May be taken concurrently).

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Engineers
courses.desc: Collecting, summarizing and displaying data. An introduction to probability theory and its applications. Conditional probabilities and expected values. Random variables and distributions. Drawing conclusions and making decisions using data: confidence intervals, hypotheses testing, comparison tests, regression, and correlation.
courses.text: Prerequisites: GEN_ENG 150 or GEN_ENG 151, MATH 220-2 . You may not enroll in both GEN_ENG 231-0 and GEN_ENG 241-0 during initial registration. This restriction will be removed after the initial registration period if capacity allows.

courses.title: Linear Algebra for Engineers
courses.desc: Solving linear systems of equations and LU factorization. Matrix/vector operations and algebra. Vector spaces and bases. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, Orthogonality, solution of least squares, and QR factorization. Singular values, singular value decomposition. Applications in science and engineering.
courses.text: Prerequisites: GEN_ENG 150 or 151, MATH 220-2 . You may not enroll in both GEN_ENG 231-0 and GEN_ENG 241-0 during initial registration. This restriction will be removed after the initial registration period if capacity allows.

courses.title: Applied Ordinary Differential Equations
courses.desc: Students will learn to identify and solve differential equations derived from scientific and engineered systems. They will also learn to formulate a differential equation for modeling suitable applications, specifically mechanical vibrations and electrical circuits, among others.
courses.text: Prerequisites: GEN_ENG 150 or GEN_ENG 151 or CS 150, MATH 220-2 , PHYS 135-1 or GEN_ENG 212 (may be taken concurrently), GEN_ENG 241 (may be taken concurrently).

courses.title: Single-Variable Differential Calculus
courses.desc: Limits. Differentiation. Linear approximation and related rates. Extreme value theorem, mean value theorem, and curve-sketching. Optimization. Students may not receive credit for both MATH 220-1 and any of MATH 211-0, MATH 212-0 (former), MATH 213-0 (former), MATH 218-1, MATH 218-2, or MATH 220-0 (former).

courses.title: Single-Variable Integral Calculus
courses.desc: Definite integrals, antiderivatives, and the fundamental theorem of calculus. Transcendental and inverse functions. Areas and volumes. Techniques of integration, numerical integration, and improper integrals. First-order linear and separable ordinary differential equations. Students may not receive credit for both MATH 220-2 and any of MATH 213-0 (former), MATH 214-0 (former), MATH 218-3, or MATH 224-0 (former).
courses.text: Prerequisite: MATH 218-2 or MATH 220-0 (former) or MATH 220-1 .

courses.title: Multivariable Differential Calculus for Engineering
courses.desc: Vectors, vector functions, partial derivatives, Taylor polynomials, and optimization. Emphasis on engineering applications. For McCormick School of Engineering students only. Students may not receive credit for both MATH 228-1 and any of MATH 230-0 (former), MATH 230-1, MATH 281-1, MATH 285-2, MATH 290-2, MATH 291-2, or ES_APPM 252-1.
courses.text: Prerequisite: MATH 218-3 or MATH 214-0 (former) or MATH 220-2 or MATH 224-0 (former).

courses.title: Multivariable Integral Calculus for Engineering
courses.desc: Multiple integration: double integrals, triple integrals, and change of variables. Vector calculus: vector fields, line integrals, surface integrals, curl and divergence, Green's theorem, Stokes' theorem, and the divergence theorem. Emphasis on engineering applications. For McCormick School of Engineering students only. Students may not receive credit for both MATH 228-2 and any of MATH 230-2, MATH 234-0 (former), MATH 281-2, MATH 285-3, MATH 290-3, MATH 291-3, or ES_APPM 252-2.
courses.text: Prerequisite: MATH 228-1 or MATH 230-0 (former) or MATH 230-1 or MATH 281-1 or MATH 285-2 or MATH 290-2 or MATH 291-2 or ES_APPM 252-1 .

courses.title: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering Principles
courses.desc: Basic concepts of Materials Science and Engineering: bonding, crystal structure, defects in solids, phase diagrams, and development of microstructures. Processing/structure/property/performance relationships underlying the behavior of metals, ceramics, polymers, semiconductors, and composites. Mechanical, electrical, and chemical properties of engineering materials. Broadly, how materials’ performance influences technological development, the economy, the environment, and society. Not to be taken for credit with or after MAT_SCI 301-0.

courses.title: Thermodynamics & Statistical Mechanics - I
courses.desc: Basic thermodynamics, applications to energy efficiency and climate change, and introduction to statistical thermodynamics.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics I
courses.desc: Fundamentals of fluid mechanics. Properties and statics of fluids. Kinematics and dynamics of fluid motion-continuity, momentum, and energy equations. Dimensional analysis, flow in closed conduits.
courses.text: Prerequisites: MATH 228-2 (may be taken concurrently) and GEN_ENG 205-4 .

courses.title: Analysis and Performance of Text
courses.desc: This course studies texts, broadly defined and situated, through performance. Students explore how performance helps the performer and audience interpret a text, as well as express challenging political and personal themes. They examine the ways performance illuminates and draws out deeper understandings of social relations through embodied praxis.

courses.title: Performance Culture and Communication
courses.desc: Explores how live performance and dramatic forms of communication are methods used to examine social behavior and cultural expressions.

courses.title: General Physics
courses.desc: Calculus-based physics for science and engineering majors and premedical students. Electricity and magnetism. Must be taken concurrently with PHYSICS 136-2.
courses.text: Prerequisites: MATH 220-1 , MATH 220-2 , MATH 230-1 OR MATH 290-1 OR MATH 291-1 , PHYSICS 135-1 ; MATH 230-2 OR MATH 290-2 OR MATH 291-2 (may be taken concurrently).".

courses.title: General Physics Laboratory
courses.desc: Introductory physics laboratory for students taking PHYSICS 130-2 or PHYSICS 135-2, with which it must be taken concurrently.

courses.title: Engineering Improv: From Allowing to Application
courses.desc: Start anywhere, remember you are not the most important person in the scene, and say yes. Through these and other improv techniques, students learn to tackle unexpected obstacles, building skills that can be leveraged in both academic and non-academic contexts to face challenges with resilience.
